      "observations": [
        "The migration makes server/folder identity strings UTF-8 to prepare for the new database, while localized display names and nsIFile filesystem operations retain their actual UTF-16 boundaries. Mbox/Maildir creators accept the UTF-8 name, retain a safe nsString for Append and convert a separate identity copy back to UTF-8. Public interface type alone does not establish physical Mork property encoding or make every protocol wire name UTF-8; reuse the existing field/wire/token lessons.",
        "Inherited empty folder string properties still fall back through parent/server defaults. Native and JS preference setters clear empty/default-valued user settings; native fallback return handling is not proof every underlying preference read succeeded. The name notification migrates to the UTF-8 property callback; removed unichar callback leaves a hole in listener flag bits. Existing named-mask tests and boundary notes remain scoped source contracts.",
        "Review proposes foo for UTF-8 and foo16 only for needed UTF-16 distinctions in this migration. The author’s Assign habit and reviewer’s personal preference do not establish a universal assignment rule. Broad nsAutoCString advice is explicitly withdrawn for this patch in favor of literal conversion; a future lint pass is only a proposal. The alternative localized-string conversion location is explicitly permitted either way.",
        "The reviewer leaves Windows path-separator behavior uncertain and suggests a parseURI test, then permits existing code. Current tests cover Windows backslash hashing and legal Unicode operations but explicitly skip escaped-slash behavior; the split-before-unescape source contract must not be described as tested by that omitted case. IMAP modified UTF-7 isolation is a follow-up proposal, not fully applied architectural separation.",
        "The author retains an unexplained historical line rather than inventing its purpose; the reviewer attributes a possible copied origin and calls it out of scope. The later Neil link supplies a locator only, not an independently read rationale. Fixed helper length/surrogate refinements and later non-ASCII Windows-hashing removal are endpoint/assigned-follow-up distinctions, not this migration’s original behavior. The full tracker lists later regressions, with no newly audited causal proof."
